notes:
STORY. Unit 7 is a brick-and-metal warehouse on a corner lot in an industrial back street; the den is its old gatehouse-office, a small brick outbuilding at the lot's street corner, 2.25 m behind both footpaths, its door opening into the lorry lane behind it and its windows onto the fenced compound beside it. Two 6 m carriageways with 15 cm kerbs and 1.5 m footpaths meet at a T just off the den's corner: the front street (z 11-17) runs along the +z side past the compound gate, the side street (x 12-18) runs up the +x side past the lot gate and the warehouse's blank east wall and dead-ends at a shed further north. The lot is one enclosure: warehouse across the back, wing down the west side, chain-link along the front street (x -17..-6.5, a 5 m double gate at x -13.5..-8.5 with a flat crossover and two bollards) closing against the den's SW corner, chain-link along the side street from the warehouse corner to a return at the den's NE corner, with a 6 m gate at z -14.5..-8.5 for the lorries; inside are the compound's containers, skip, drums, scrap and two sodium posts, the reversing lane with its beacon and cones, the door cluster, and the lit bay in line with the door. Across the front street: a small flat-roofed joinery (Unit A) with its roller doors turned to its side forecourt, then a vacant lot with weeds, dumped tyres, a blank hoarding and two jersey barriers across its old crossover, a bus bench and flag on the far footpath, a line of wooden power poles at 10 m and sodium columns at 12 m along it. Across the side street: a single-storey unit with a roller door, a bin and a flatbed on its hardstand. By day everything outside is the grey wash and the kit's grey asphalt; at night four street columns, the yard's three posts, the den's three LEDs, the bay, two floods and the beacon are the only colour, with the two tags, three cones and one hydrant as the daytime accents.

SCORES (a real place / b foreground+door / c tiles / d pieces exist / e simple+grey / f den focus = total): plan 1: 9/8/9/7/6/8 = 47. plan 2: 8/7/7/9/5/7 = 43. plan 3: 7/8/8/8/8/8 = 47. Plan 1 is the base (the corner lot at a T reads as a place; kerbs on the 3 m facade grid; footpaths, crossovers, bus stop, pole line, a unit across each street). Its faults: pieces named that are not converted (ad-board, trashcan_kenney, electricity-pole-wide, signs at 8), a 70-prop list, and two sightlines that assume an eye-level view (a 35 deg camera sees only ground through the windows). Plan 3 ties on points for its engineering (tile levels, ramp thinking, correct window/door ray maths, trimming the warehouse at the boundary) but has one street and dirt on the +z side. Plan 2's 8 m city tiles give 0.8 m footpaths and a colormap the wash flattens to one grey, its near-side power pole stands 4 m from the plinth corner, its sign board is 1.9 m at 7 m, and it spends 16 lights and 24 pieces on Unit A/B.

VERIFIED FROM THE SOURCE GLBS (index buffers, not bboxes): asphalt_side = flat asphalt on local z -0.5..0 and a 0.05-unit (0.15 m at scale 3) raised concreteSmooth block on local z 0..+0.5; asphalt_corner_outer = a raised quarter-disc r 0.5 in the local +x+z corner, asphalt elsewhere; asphalt_center/pavement are zero-thickness quads. So: yaw 180 = pavement toward -z, yaw 0 = +z, yaw -90 = -x, yaw 90 = +x; corner-outer yaw 180 = disc toward -x-z, yaw 90 = +x-z. The 84 tiles were generated and machine-checked: all on the grid (x edges 10.5+3k, z edges 9.5+3k), no overlaps, no holes in any row or column, kerb lines continuous into the corner arcs. shed cubes: the garage/door/window face is local -z. light-curved/light-square arms point local -z; after --recenter the shaft sits at local +z 0.77 (street_light) / 0.72 (lamp_post). electricity-pole-single: single pole, crossarm along local z. Retro-urban materials are textured (colormap) so an un-washed tile shows the kit's greys, a washed one goes flat 0.48.

WHAT CHANGED FROM PLAN 1: (1) Grid shifted so the lot boundary is the back edge of the kerb tile (footpath z 9.5-11 / x 10.5-12, kerb at z 11 / x 12, carriageway z 11-17 / x 12-18): the 1.5 m raised half IS the footpath, so no footpath primitives and nothing has to be lifted (WorldSite places every tile at one height). (2) Compound simplified per plan 3's spirit: no internal fence at x -9; the whole lot is one enclosure with the wing and warehouse as two sides, 9 fence segments instead of 6 runs plus 12 old panels; two short returns tie the fence to the den's SW and NE plinth corners so the yard is actually closed. (3) Unit A grafted from plan 2 but as 6 flat-topped shed cubes (roof wedges cannot be stacked by the builder); its doors face +x. (4) Low unit across the side street as 5 cubes (solid, seen from two sides) instead of single-sided tiles with primitive roof boxes. (5) Poles as single poles at 10 m (plan 3's spacing), phased at x -18,-8,2,12,22 so none coincides on screen with a column or the bus stop; wires go in WorldYard. (6) Street columns are the 6 m curved street_light (already converted), not lamp_post, so the municipal street and the yard's square posts read as two families; only the four in-frame heads are light sources. (7) Bus stop kept (bench + blank sign), bench moved onto the pavement; street bin dropped (no suitable piece). (8) Hoarding is the converted billboard (sign-highway @7), not ad-board; signs at scale 6. (9) Drains, manholes, bollards and the hydrant use WorldSite's primitives; puddles are not placed on tiles (a puddle at -0.129 would be under the tile top at -0.12). (10) Lorry left where it is (plan 1's move collided with the tank and drums); scaffold pair, both jersey barriers and the white bay stripes dropped rather than re-homed. (11) Distant pieces cut to two since the frame never reaches the horizon. (12) Areas avoid the word 'lot' where dirt is meant (the builder's keyword switch maps 'lot' to asphalt 0.30). (13) Every table entry is an ADDITION placed by WorldSite; nothing already in WorldYard is repeated, so the tables cannot duplicate pieces.
